payload.name: Container Resource Limit and Secret Permission Gaps
payload.description: Launching sandbox containers without explicit CPU, memory, and PID limits or staging secret and credential files with overly permissive modes or raw env-file exposure risks host resource exhaustion and credential leakage.
symptoms: Runaway container processes starving host CPU, memory, or process table capacity
Temporary env or credential files created with group/world-readable permissions instead of 0600
Secrets exposed in process command-line arguments or retained on disk after container exit
root_causes: Omitting explicit Docker resource constraint flags such as --cpus, --memory, and PID limits in container launch builders
Creating secret files with default umask permissions instead of enforcing 0600 modes
Passing sensitive tokens through unguarded environment files or CLI flags without cleanup

mitigations.description: Always pass explicit --cpus, --memory, and process limit flags when constructing container launch commands.
Create staged secret files with 0600 permissions, avoid CLI-arg token exposure, remove temporary files on exit, and cover launcher/credential boundaries with hermetic unit tests.
